title: Sum of Two Numbers
statement: Given two integers a and b, print their sum.
inputFormat: A single line containing two space-separated integers a and b.
outputFormat: A single integer — the sum of a and b.

title: Reverse a String
statement: Given a string s, print the string reversed.
inputFormat: A single line containing the string s.
outputFormat: The reversed string.

title: FizzBuzz
statement: Print the numbers from 1 to n, one per line. For multiples of 3 print "Fizz" instead of the number, for multiples of 5 print "Buzz", and for multiples of both print "FizzBuzz".
inputFormat: A single integer n.
outputFormat: n lines, each containing a number, Fizz, Buzz, or FizzBuzz.

2

Buzz

7

FizzBuzz

title: Maximum in an Array
statement: Given an array of n integers, print the largest element.
inputFormat: The first line contains n. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: A single integer — the maximum element.

title: Count Vowels
statement: Given a string s, count how many characters are vowels (a, e, i, o, u — in either case).
inputFormat: A single line containing the string s.
outputFormat: A single integer — the number of vowels.

title: Factorial
statement: Given a non-negative integer n, print n! (n factorial). Note that 0! = 1.
inputFormat: A single integer n.
outputFormat: A single integer — the value of n!.

title: GCD of Two Numbers
statement: Given two positive integers a and b, print their greatest common divisor.
inputFormat: A single line containing two space-separated integers a and b.
outputFormat: A single integer — gcd(a, b).

title: Check Palindrome
statement: Given a string s, determine whether it reads the same forwards and backwards. Print YES if it does, otherwise print NO.
inputFormat: A single line containing the string s.
outputFormat: YES or NO.

title: Binary Search
statement: Given a sorted array of n distinct integers and a target value, print the 0-based index of the target, or -1 if it is not present.
constraints: 1 <= n <= 10^5. The array is sorted in strictly increasing order.
inputFormat: The first line contains n. The second line contains n sorted integers. The third line contains the target.
outputFormat: The 0-based index of the target, or -1.

title: Nth Fibonacci Number
statement: Print the nth Fibonacci number, where F(1) = 1, F(2) = 1, and F(n) = F(n-1) + F(n-2).
constraints: 1 <= n <= 90. The answer fits in a 64-bit signed integer.
inputFormat: A single integer n.
outputFormat: A single integer — F(n).

title: Longest Common Prefix
statement: Given n strings, print the longest common prefix shared by all of them. If there is no common prefix, print -1.
inputFormat: The first line contains n. The next n lines each contain one string.
outputFormat: The longest common prefix, or -1 if there is none.

title: Two Sum Indices
statement: Given an array of n integers and a target, find the two distinct positions whose values add up to the target. Print their 0-based indices in increasing order. Exactly one valid answer exists.
constraints: 2 <= n <= 10^5. Exactly one valid pair exists.
inputFormat: The first line contains n. The second line contains n integers. The third line contains the target.
outputFormat: Two space-separated 0-based indices, smaller first.

title: Spiral Matrix Traversal
statement: Given an n x m matrix, print all its elements in spiral order, starting from the top-left corner and moving clockwise.
inputFormat: The first line contains n and m. The next n lines each contain m integers.
outputFormat: All n*m elements in spiral order, space-separated on one line.

title: 0/1 Knapsack
statement: You are given n items, each with a weight and a value, and a knapsack with capacity W. Each item may be taken at most once. Print the maximum total value you can carry without exceeding the capacity.
inputFormat: The first line contains n and W. The next n lines each contain the weight and value of one item.
outputFormat: A single integer — the maximum achievable value.

title: Longest Increasing Subsequence
statement: Given an array of n integers, print the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence. A subsequence need not be contiguous.
inputFormat: The first line contains n. The second line contains n integers.
outputFormat: A single integer — the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence.

title: Array Sum
statement: You are given an array of n integers. Print the sum of all its elements.
inputFormat: The first line contains an integer n. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: A single integer — the sum of the array.

title: Second Largest Element
statement: Given an array of n integers, find the second largest distinct value in it. If every element is the same, so that no second distinct value exists, print -1.
inputFormat: The first line contains an integer n. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: The second largest distinct value, or -1 if there is none.

title: Count Even and Odd
statement: Given an array of n integers, count how many of them are even and how many are odd. Note that negative numbers can be even too.
inputFormat: The first line contains an integer n. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: Two space-separated integers: the count of even numbers followed by the count of odd numbers.

title: Reverse an Array
statement: Given an array of n integers, print its elements in reverse order.
inputFormat: The first line contains an integer n. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: n space-separated integers — the array in reverse order.

title: Linear Search
statement: Given an array of n integers and a target value x, print the 1-based index of the first occurrence of x in the array. If x does not appear, print -1.
inputFormat: The first line contains two integers n and x. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: The 1-based index of the first occurrence of x, or -1.

title: Sum of Even Numbers
statement: Given an array of n integers, print the sum of only the even-valued elements. If there are none, print 0.
inputFormat: The first line contains an integer n. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: A single integer — the sum of the even elements.

title: Minimum and Maximum
statement: Given an array of n integers, print its smallest and largest elements.
inputFormat: The first line contains an integer n. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: Two space-separated integers: the minimum followed by the maximum.

title: Count Occurrences
statement: Given an array of n integers and a value x, count how many times x appears in the array.
inputFormat: The first line contains two integers n and x. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: A single integer — the number of occurrences of x.

title: Array Average
statement: Given an array of n integers, print their average rounded to exactly two decimal places. Standard rounding applies.
inputFormat: The first line contains an integer n. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: The average, printed with exactly two digits after the decimal point.

title: Move Zeros to End
statement: Given an array of n integers, move every zero to the end of the array while keeping the relative order of the non-zero elements unchanged. Print the resulting array.
inputFormat: The first line contains an integer n. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: n space-separated integers — the rearranged array.

title: Prefix Sum Queries
statement:
You are given an array of n integers and q queries. Each query gives two indices l and r (1-based, inclusive) and asks for the sum of the elements in that range. Answer every query.

A naive scan per query is too slow for the largest inputs — precompute prefix sums so each query is answered in constant time.
inputFormat: The first line contains two integers n and q. The second line contains n space-separated integers. Each of the next q lines contains two integers l and r.
outputFormat: q lines, each the answer to the corresponding query.

title: Rotate Array Left
statement: Given an array of n integers, rotate it k positions to the left and print the result. Rotating left by one moves the first element to the end. Note that k may be larger than n.
inputFormat: The first line contains two integers n and k. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: n space-separated integers — the rotated array.

title: Remove Duplicates from Sorted Array
statement: You are given a sorted array of n integers in non-decreasing order. Print the array with duplicates removed, keeping the order.
constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000
-10^9 <= a[i] <= 10^9
The array is given in non-decreasing order.
inputFormat: The first line contains an integer n. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: The distinct values in increasing order, space-separated.

title: Maximum Subarray Sum
statement:
Given an array of n integers, find the largest sum obtainable from any contiguous non-empty subarray.

For example, in [-2, 1, -3, 4, -1, 2, 1, -5, 4] the best contiguous block is [4, -1, 2, 1], which sums to 6.
inputFormat: The first line contains an integer n. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: A single integer — the maximum subarray sum.

title: Equilibrium Index
statement:
An equilibrium index of an array is a position where the sum of all elements strictly to its left equals the sum of all elements strictly to its right. Print the smallest 1-based equilibrium index, or -1 if there is none.

An empty side sums to 0, so the first and last positions are eligible.
inputFormat: The first line contains an integer n. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: The smallest 1-based equilibrium index, or -1.

title: Missing Number
statement: The array contains n distinct integers drawn from the range 1 to n+1, so exactly one value in that range is absent. Find it.
constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000
All values are distinct and lie between 1 and n+1.
inputFormat: The first line contains an integer n. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: The missing value.

title: Sort an Array
statement: Given an array of n integers, print its elements sorted in non-decreasing order.
inputFormat: The first line contains an integer n. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: n space-separated integers in non-decreasing order.

title: Kth Smallest Element
statement: Given an array of n integers and a number k, print the kth smallest element. Duplicates count separately, so in [3, 1, 1, 2] the 2nd smallest is 1.
inputFormat: The first line contains two integers n and k. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: The kth smallest element.

title: Pair with Given Sum
statement: Given an array of n integers and a target sum s, decide whether some two distinct positions hold values adding up to s. Print YES or NO.
inputFormat: The first line contains two integers n and s. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: YES if such a pair exists, otherwise NO.

title: Majority Element
statement: An element is a majority element if it occurs strictly more than n/2 times. Given an array of n integers, print the majority element, or -1 if none exists.
inputFormat: The first line contains an integer n. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: The majority element, or -1.

title: Product of Array Except Self
statement:
Given an array of n integers, print an array in which position i holds the product of every element except a[i]. Because the products can be enormous, print each value modulo 1000000007.

Watch out for zeros — division is not available under a modulus unless the divisor is invertible, so build the answer from prefix and suffix products instead.
inputFormat: The first line contains an integer n. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: n space-separated integers, each taken modulo 1000000007.

title: Merge Two Sorted Arrays
statement: You are given two arrays that are each already sorted in non-decreasing order. Merge them into a single sorted array and print it.
constraints:
1 <= n, m <= 100000
-10^9 <= values <= 10^9
Both arrays are given in non-decreasing order.
inputFormat: The first line contains two integers n and m. The second line contains n integers. The third line contains m integers.
outputFormat: n + m space-separated integers in non-decreasing order.

title: Longest Consecutive Run
statement: Given an array of n integers, find the length of the longest run of equal values appearing next to each other.
inputFormat: The first line contains an integer n. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: A single integer — the length of the longest run.

title: Frequency of Each Element
statement: Given an array of n integers, print each distinct value together with how many times it occurs, in increasing order of value.
inputFormat: The first line contains an integer n. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: One line per distinct value: the value, a space, then its count. Values in increasing order.

title: Trapping Rain Water
statement:
An array of n non-negative integers describes an elevation map where each bar has width 1. After it rains, water settles in the dips. Compute how many units of water are trapped.

Water above position i is limited by the tallest bar to its left and the tallest to its right — specifically by the smaller of those two, minus the height at i.
inputFormat: The first line contains an integer n. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: A single integer — the total units of trapped water.

title: String Length
statement: Given a string of lowercase letters, print how many characters it contains.
constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 100000
s consists of lowercase English letters.
inputFormat: A single line containing the string s.
outputFormat: A single integer — the length of s.

title: Convert to Uppercase
statement: Given a string of lowercase letters, print it converted to uppercase.
constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 100000
s consists of lowercase English letters.
inputFormat: A single line containing the string s.
outputFormat: The string in uppercase.

title: Count Character Occurrences
statement: Given a string s and a character c, count how many times c appears in s.
constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 100000
s consists of lowercase English letters, and c is a lowercase letter.
inputFormat: The first line contains the string s. The second line contains the single character c.
outputFormat: A single integer — the number of occurrences.

title: Remove Duplicate Characters
statement: Given a string of lowercase letters, print it with every repeated character removed, keeping only the first appearance of each and preserving the original order.
constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 100000
s consists of lowercase English letters.
inputFormat: A single line containing the string s.
outputFormat: The string with duplicate characters removed.

title: Check Anagram
statement: Two strings are anagrams when one can be rearranged into the other, using exactly the same letters the same number of times. Given two strings, print YES if they are anagrams and NO otherwise.
constraints:
1 <= |a|, |b| <= 100000
Both strings consist of lowercase English letters.
inputFormat: Two lines, each containing one string.
outputFormat: YES or NO.

title: Reverse Words in a Sentence
statement: Given a sentence made of words separated by single spaces, print the words in reverse order, still separated by single spaces.
constraints:
1 <= number of words <= 10000
Each word consists of lowercase English letters, length at most 20.
inputFormat: A single line containing the sentence.
outputFormat: The words in reverse order, separated by single spaces.

title: First Non-Repeating Character
statement: Given a string of lowercase letters, print the first character that appears exactly once. If every character repeats, print -1.
constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 100000
s consists of lowercase English letters.
inputFormat: A single line containing the string s.
outputFormat: The first non-repeating character, or -1.

title: Longest Word in a Sentence
statement: Given a sentence of words separated by single spaces, print the longest word. If several words tie for the longest, print the one that appears first.
constraints:
1 <= number of words <= 10000
Each word consists of lowercase English letters, length at most 20.
inputFormat: A single line containing the sentence.
outputFormat: The longest word.

title: Palindrome Sentence
statement: A string reads as a palindrome if it is the same forwards and backwards once you ignore everything that is not a letter or digit and treat uppercase and lowercase as equal. Given a line of text, print YES if it is a palindrome under those rules, otherwise NO.
constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 100000
s contains printable ASCII characters and may include spaces.
inputFormat: A single line of text.
outputFormat: YES or NO.
sampleInput: A man a plan a canal Panama

testCases.input: A man a plan a canal Panama

title: Count Words
statement: Given a line of text containing words separated by one or more spaces, count how many words it contains.
inputFormat: A single line of text.
outputFormat: A single integer — the number of words.

title: String Compression
statement: Compress a string by replacing each run of the same character with that character followed by the run length. For example aaabbc becomes a3b2c1. Print the compressed form even when it is longer than the original.
constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 100000
s consists of lowercase English letters.
inputFormat: A single line containing the string s.
outputFormat: The compressed string.

title: Substring Search
statement: Given a text string s and a pattern p, print the 1-based index where p first occurs inside s, or -1 if it does not occur at all.
constraints:
1 <= |p| <= |s| <= 100000
Both strings consist of lowercase English letters.
inputFormat: The first line contains s. The second line contains p.
outputFormat: The 1-based starting index of the first occurrence, or -1.

title: Vowel and Consonant Count
statement: Given a string of lowercase letters, print how many vowels and how many consonants it contains.
constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 100000
s consists of lowercase English letters.
inputFormat: A single line containing the string s.
outputFormat: Two space-separated integers: the vowel count followed by the consonant count.

title: Capitalize Each Word
statement: Given a sentence of lowercase words separated by single spaces, print it with the first letter of every word capitalised.
constraints:
1 <= number of words <= 10000
Each word consists of lowercase English letters, length at most 20.
inputFormat: A single line containing the sentence.
outputFormat: The sentence with each word capitalised.

title: Longest Substring Without Repeating Characters
statement:
Given a string of lowercase letters, find the length of the longest contiguous block in which no character repeats.

A sliding window works well here: extend the right edge, and whenever a repeat appears, pull the left edge past the previous occurrence of that character.
constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 100000
s consists of lowercase English letters.
inputFormat: A single line containing the string s.
outputFormat: A single integer — the length of the longest such block.

title: Valid Parentheses
statement: A bracket string is balanced when every opening bracket is closed by the matching kind in the right order. Given a string made of the characters ()[]{}, print YES if it is balanced and NO otherwise.
constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 100000
s consists only of the characters ( ) [ ] { }
inputFormat: A single line containing the string s.
outputFormat: YES or NO.

title: Count Distinct Characters
statement: Given a string of lowercase letters, count how many distinct characters it uses.
constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 100000
s consists of lowercase English letters.
inputFormat: A single line containing the string s.
outputFormat: A single integer — the number of distinct characters.

title: Run Length Decoding
statement: A string has been encoded as a sequence of a letter followed by a count, for example a3b2 meaning aaabb. Given such an encoding, print the original string.
constraints:
The encoded string has length at most 2000.
Each count is between 1 and 50 and every letter is lowercase.
inputFormat: A single line containing the encoded string.
outputFormat: The decoded string.

title: Rotate String Check
statement: Given two strings a and b, decide whether b can be obtained by rotating a. Rotating means moving some number of characters from the front to the back, so abcde rotated by 2 gives cdeab. Print YES or NO.
constraints:
1 <= |a|, |b| <= 100000
Both strings consist of lowercase English letters.
inputFormat: Two lines, each containing one string.
outputFormat: YES or NO.

title: Character Frequency Sort
statement: Given a string of lowercase letters, print its characters sorted by how often they occur, most frequent first. Characters that occur equally often must appear in alphabetical order relative to one another, and each character is printed as many times as it occurs.
constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 100000
s consists of lowercase English letters.
inputFormat: A single line containing the string s.
outputFormat: The rearranged string.

title: Longest Common Substring Length
statement:
Given two strings, find the length of the longest contiguous block of characters that appears in both.

Note that this asks for a *substring* (contiguous), not a subsequence.
constraints:
1 <= |a|, |b| <= 1000
Both strings consist of lowercase English letters.
inputFormat: Two lines, each containing one string.
outputFormat: A single integer — the length of the longest common substring.

title: Isomorphic Strings
statement: Two strings are isomorphic when the characters of the first can be consistently replaced to produce the second: every occurrence of a given character must map to the same character, and no two different characters may map to the same one. Print YES or NO.
constraints:
1 <= |a|, |b| <= 100000
Both strings consist of lowercase English letters.
inputFormat: Two lines, each containing one string.
outputFormat: YES or NO.

title: Word Frequency Report
statement: Given a line of lowercase words separated by single spaces, print each distinct word with the number of times it appears, ordered alphabetically.
constraints:
1 <= number of words <= 10000
Each word consists of lowercase English letters, length at most 20.
inputFormat: A single line containing the sentence.
outputFormat: One line per distinct word: the word, a space, then its count, in alphabetical order.

title: Check Prime
statement: Given an integer n, print YES if it is prime and NO otherwise. Recall that 1 is not prime.
inputFormat: A single line containing the integer n.
outputFormat: YES or NO.

title: Sum of Digits
statement: Given a non-negative integer n, print the sum of its decimal digits.
inputFormat: A single line containing the integer n.
outputFormat: A single integer — the digit sum.

title: Count Digits
statement: Given a non-negative integer n, print how many decimal digits it has. The number 0 has one digit.
inputFormat: A single line containing the integer n.
outputFormat: A single integer — the number of digits.

title: Power with Modulo
statement: Given integers a, b and m, compute a raised to the power b, modulo m. The exponent can be very large, so repeated multiplication is far too slow — use fast exponentiation by squaring.
inputFormat: A single line containing three integers a, b and m.
outputFormat: A single integer — a^b mod m.

title: LCM of Two Numbers
statement: Given two positive integers a and b, print their least common multiple.
inputFormat: A single line containing two integers a and b.
outputFormat: A single integer — the least common multiple.

title: Count Divisors
statement: Given a positive integer n, count how many positive integers divide it exactly.
inputFormat: A single line containing the integer n.
outputFormat: A single integer — the number of divisors.

title: Sum of First N Natural Numbers
statement: Given a positive integer n, print the sum 1 + 2 + ... + n. Note that n can be large enough that a loop is fine but the result will not fit in 32 bits.
inputFormat: A single line containing the integer n.
outputFormat: A single integer — the sum.

title: Perfect Number
statement: A perfect number equals the sum of its positive divisors excluding itself — 6 = 1 + 2 + 3, for example. Given n, print YES if it is perfect and NO otherwise.
inputFormat: A single line containing the integer n.
outputFormat: YES or NO.

title: Armstrong Number
statement: An Armstrong number of d digits equals the sum of its digits each raised to the power d. For instance 153 has three digits and 1^3 + 5^3 + 3^3 = 153. Print YES or NO.
inputFormat: A single line containing the integer n.
outputFormat: YES or NO.

title: Reverse a Number
statement: Given a non-negative integer n, print the number formed by reversing its decimal digits. Leading zeros in the result are dropped, so 100 becomes 1.
inputFormat: A single line containing the integer n.
outputFormat: A single integer — the reversed number.

title: Prime Factorisation
statement: Given an integer n greater than 1, print its prime factors in increasing order, one per line, each followed by how many times it divides n.
inputFormat: A single line containing the integer n.
outputFormat: One line per distinct prime factor: the prime, a space, then its exponent.

title: Sieve of Eratosthenes
statement: Given an integer n, count how many prime numbers are less than or equal to n. For the larger inputs a per-number primality test is too slow — sieve instead.
inputFormat: A single line containing the integer n.
outputFormat: A single integer — the count of primes up to and including n.

title: Binary Representation
statement: Given a non-negative integer n, print its binary representation without leading zeros.
inputFormat: A single line containing the integer n.
outputFormat: The binary representation of n.

title: Count Set Bits
statement: Given a non-negative integer n, count how many bits are set to 1 in its binary representation.
inputFormat: A single line containing the integer n.
outputFormat: A single integer — the number of set bits.

title: Power of Two
statement: Given a positive integer n, print YES if it is an exact power of two and NO otherwise.
inputFormat: A single line containing the integer n.
outputFormat: YES or NO.

title: Decimal to Base Conversion
statement: Given a non-negative integer n and a base b between 2 and 16, print n written in base b. Digits above nine are written as the uppercase letters A to F.
inputFormat: A single line containing two integers n and b.
outputFormat: n expressed in base b.

title: Nth Prime Number
statement: Given a positive integer n, print the nth prime number. The first prime is 2.
inputFormat: A single line containing the integer n.
outputFormat: A single integer — the nth prime.

title: Happy Number
statement: Repeatedly replace a number by the sum of the squares of its digits. If this eventually reaches 1 the number is happy; otherwise it falls into a cycle. Given n, print YES if it is happy and NO otherwise.
inputFormat: A single line containing the integer n.
outputFormat: YES or NO.

title: Trailing Zeros in Factorial
statement: Given n, count the trailing zeros of n factorial. Computing the factorial outright is hopeless for large n — count the factors of five instead.
inputFormat: A single line containing the integer n.
outputFormat: A single integer — the number of trailing zeros.

title: Modular Inverse
statement:
Given an integer a and a prime p, find the modular inverse of a modulo p — the value x in the range 0 to p-1 with a*x congruent to 1 modulo p. If a is divisible by p no inverse exists, so print -1.

Since p is prime, Fermat’s little theorem gives the inverse directly as a^(p-2) mod p.
inputFormat: A single line containing two integers a and p.
outputFormat: The modular inverse of a modulo p, or -1.

title: Sum of Squares
statement: Given a positive integer n, print 1^2 + 2^2 + ... + n^2.
inputFormat: A single line containing the integer n.
outputFormat: A single integer — the sum of squares.

title: Collatz Steps
statement: Starting from n, repeatedly halve it when even and replace it by 3n+1 when odd, until it reaches 1. Print how many steps this takes. Starting at 1 takes zero steps.
inputFormat: A single line containing the integer n.
outputFormat: A single integer — the number of steps to reach 1.

title: Binomial Coefficient
statement:
Given n and r, compute the number of ways to choose r items from n, modulo 1000000007.

Precompute factorials and use modular inverses; computing the factorials directly overflows long before n reaches its limit.
inputFormat: A single line containing two integers n and r.
outputFormat: The binomial coefficient modulo 1000000007.

title: Digital Root
statement: Repeatedly replace a number by the sum of its digits until a single digit remains, and print that digit.
inputFormat: A single line containing the integer n.
outputFormat: A single digit — the digital root.

title: Climbing Stairs
statement: A staircase has n steps and you may climb either one or two steps at a time. Count the distinct ways to reach the top, modulo 1000000007.
inputFormat: A single line containing the integer n.
outputFormat: The number of ways, modulo 1000000007.

title: Coin Change Minimum Coins
statement: Given coin denominations and a target amount, find the fewest coins that add up exactly to the amount. Coins may be reused freely. If the amount cannot be formed, print -1.
inputFormat: The first line contains two integers n and amount. The second line contains n space-separated coin values.
outputFormat: The minimum number of coins, or -1.

title: Coin Change Number of Ways
statement: Given coin denominations and a target amount, count the distinct combinations of coins that sum to the amount. Order does not matter, so 1+2 and 2+1 count once. Print the answer modulo 1000000007.
inputFormat: The first line contains two integers n and amount. The second line contains n space-separated coin values.
outputFormat: The number of combinations, modulo 1000000007.

title: House Robber
statement: Each house on a street holds some amount of money, but taking from two adjacent houses triggers an alarm. Find the largest total you can take without ever taking from two neighbours.
inputFormat: The first line contains an integer n. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: A single integer — the maximum total.

title: Minimum Path Sum in a Grid
statement: You start at the top-left cell of an n by m grid of non-negative numbers and must reach the bottom-right, moving only right or down. Find the smallest possible sum of the cells you pass through, including both endpoints.
inputFormat: The first line contains n and m. The next n lines each contain m integers.
outputFormat: A single integer — the minimum path sum.

title: Unique Paths in a Grid
statement: Count the distinct routes from the top-left to the bottom-right of an n by m grid when you may only move right or down. Print the answer modulo 1000000007.
inputFormat: A single line containing two integers n and m.
outputFormat: The number of paths, modulo 1000000007.

title: Edit Distance
statement: Find the fewest single-character edits — insertions, deletions or substitutions — needed to turn the first string into the second.
constraints:
1 <= |a|, |b| <= 2000
Both strings consist of lowercase English letters.
inputFormat: Two lines, each containing one string.
outputFormat: A single integer — the edit distance.

title: Longest Common Subsequence
statement: Find the length of the longest sequence of characters appearing in both strings in the same relative order. The characters need not be adjacent.
constraints:
1 <= |a|, |b| <= 2000
Both strings consist of lowercase English letters.
inputFormat: Two lines, each containing one string.
outputFormat: A single integer — the length of the longest common subsequence.

title: Subset Sum Exists
statement: Given n non-negative integers and a target s, decide whether some subset of them adds up to exactly s. The empty subset sums to 0. Print YES or NO.
inputFormat: The first line contains n and s. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: YES or NO.

title: Activity Selection
statement:
You are given n activities, each with a start and finish time, and you can only do one at a time. Find the largest number of activities you can complete.

Sorting by finish time and greedily taking whatever fits is optimal here.
inputFormat: The first line contains n. Each of the next n lines contains two integers: a start and a finish time.
outputFormat: A single integer — the maximum number of activities.

title: Fractional Knapsack
statement: You have a bag of capacity W and n items, each with a weight and a value. Unlike the classic knapsack you may take fractions of an item. Print the greatest total value achievable, rounded to exactly two decimal places.
inputFormat: The first line contains n and W. Each of the next n lines contains an item weight and value.
outputFormat: The maximum value, with exactly two digits after the decimal point.

title: Minimum Platforms
statement: Given the arrival and departure times of n trains at a station, find the smallest number of platforms needed so that no train ever waits. A train arriving exactly when another departs still needs its own platform.
inputFormat: The first line contains n. The second line contains n arrival times. The third line contains n departure times.
outputFormat: A single integer — the minimum number of platforms.

title: Job Sequencing with Deadlines
statement: Each of n jobs takes one unit of time, has a deadline and pays a profit if finished by that deadline. Only one job runs at a time and time starts at 1. Choose jobs to maximise total profit.
inputFormat: The first line contains n. Each of the next n lines contains a deadline and a profit.
outputFormat: A single integer — the maximum total profit.

title: Search in Rotated Sorted Array
statement: A sorted array of distinct integers has been rotated at some unknown pivot, so [1,2,3,4,5] might have become [3,4,5,1,2]. Given the rotated array and a target, print the 1-based index of the target, or -1 if it is absent. Your solution should not simply scan every element.
constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000
All values are distinct.
-10^9 <= a[i], target <= 10^9
inputFormat: The first line contains n and the target. The second line contains the n rotated values.
outputFormat: The 1-based index of the target, or -1.

title: First and Last Position
statement: Given a sorted array and a target, print the 1-based indices of the first and last occurrence of the target, separated by a space. If it does not occur, print "-1 -1".
constraints:
1 <= n <= 100000
-10^9 <= a[i], target <= 10^9
The array is sorted in non-decreasing order.
inputFormat: The first line contains n and the target. The second line contains the n sorted values.
outputFormat: Two space-separated integers, or -1 -1.

title: Square Root by Binary Search
statement: Given a non-negative integer n, print the largest integer whose square does not exceed n — that is, the integer part of its square root.
inputFormat: A single line containing the integer n.
outputFormat: A single integer — the floor of the square root of n.

title: Aggressive Cows
statement:
You are given the positions of n stalls along a line and must place k cows in distinct stalls so that the smallest distance between any two cows is as large as possible. Print that largest possible minimum distance.

Binary search on the answer: for a candidate distance, greedily place cows and check whether all k fit.
inputFormat: The first line contains n and k. The second line contains the n stall positions.
outputFormat: A single integer — the largest possible minimum distance.

title: Tower of Hanoi Moves
statement: Count the minimum number of moves needed to shift n discs from one peg to another in the Tower of Hanoi, printing the answer modulo 1000000007.
inputFormat: A single line containing the integer n.
outputFormat: The minimum number of moves, modulo 1000000007.

title: Generate Balanced Parentheses
statement: Given n, print every balanced string of n pairs of round brackets, in lexicographic order with "(" considered smaller than ")". Print one string per line.
inputFormat: A single line containing the integer n.
outputFormat: All balanced bracket strings of n pairs, one per line, in lexicographic order.

title: Count Subsets with Given Sum
statement: Given n non-negative integers and a target s, count the subsets whose elements add up to exactly s. Two subsets are different if they use different positions, even when the values match. Print the count modulo 1000000007.
inputFormat: The first line contains n and s. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: The number of subsets, modulo 1000000007.

title: Maximum Product Subarray
statement:
Given an array of integers, find the largest product obtainable from any contiguous non-empty subarray.

Negatives make this trickier than the sum version: a very negative running product can become the best one after another negative, so track both the running maximum and the running minimum.
inputFormat: The first line contains an integer n. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: A single integer — the maximum product.

title: Longest Palindromic Substring Length
statement: Given a string of lowercase letters, find the length of the longest contiguous block that reads the same forwards and backwards.
constraints:
1 <= |s| <= 5000
s consists of lowercase English letters.
inputFormat: A single line containing the string s.
outputFormat: A single integer — the length of the longest palindromic substring.

title: Partition Equal Subset Sum
statement: Given n positive integers, decide whether they can be split into two groups with equal totals. Print YES or NO.
inputFormat: The first line contains an integer n. The second line contains n space-separated integers.
outputFormat: YES or NO.

title: Number of Islands
statement: A grid of 0s and 1s represents water and land. An island is a group of 1s connected horizontally or vertically — diagonals do not connect. Count the islands.
constraints:
1 <= n, m <= 500
Each cell is 0 or 1.
inputFormat: The first line contains n and m. The next n lines each contain m characters with no spaces.
outputFormat: A single integer — the number of islands.
